sources.title: Alan D. Sokal, A really simple elementary proof of the uniform boundedness theorem (arXiv v2, 29 December 2010)
sources.locator: Complete five-page paper read: pp.1–5, theorem and Lemma on p.2, equations (1)–(2), full gliding-hump proof; Remarks 1–7 on p.3; references pp.3–5.

contents.name: Two-sign inequality, equation (2)
contents.support: Exact inequality extracted from the displayed argument; boundedness is retained although not needed for this algebraic step.

contents.name: Uniform boundedness theorem and its elementary proof
contents.locator: p.2, theorem and proof after Lemma
contents.support: Sequence specialization with independent near-norming vectors and deterministic sign recursion added locally. Source supplies 4^n, 3^(−n), tail 3^(−n)/2 and divergent orbit; it does not supply the local AC_omega-only bookkeeping.

contents.name: Local ball lower bound, equation (1)
contents.reason: The proof only needs its two-sign inequality, retained as an A lemma. Taking a supremum over a moving ball would introduce avoidable dependent selections; the complete ball statement is already on the earlier Sokal page and is not an owned dependency.

contents.name: Remark 1: sequences versus series
contents.support: Use finite partial sums and an explicit Cauchy-tail bound. No general series equivalence is assumed.

contents.name: Remark 2: quantitative sharpness via Ball
contents.reason: The sharper reciprocal-norm summability criterion requires the plank theorem; this pair is the designated countable-choice sequential UBP supplier, not a sharp quantitative plank-theorem development.

contents.name: Remarks 3–4 and 7: alternative proofs, survey and history
contents.reason: These are bibliographic directions and historical comparisons, not additional proof obligations for the specified sequential theorem; no unread referenced work is imported.

contents.name: Remark 5: nonmeager testing set
contents.reason: The stronger category version uses the Baire machinery whose choice strength is intentionally excluded from this sharp sequential contract.

contents.name: Remark 6: nonnormable topological vector spaces
contents.reason: The source leaves extension of this proof to general topological vector spaces open; the owned theorem has a normed codomain and no locally convex generalization.

sources.title: Andrew Lin and Casey Rodriguez, MIT 18.102 Complete Lecture Notes, Spring 2021
sources.locator: Complete relevant passages read in the 125-page notes: Definition 14, Example 15, Theorem 16 and following c_0 exercise, printed pp.5–6 (PDF pp.5–6); Theorem 36 and entire proof, printed p.17 (PDF p.17).

contents.name: Definition 14: Banach space
contents.support: Sequential completeness for the norm metric, over R or C.

contents.name: Example 15: scalar and finite-dimensional completeness
contents.support: Only scalar completeness is used; the example strategy supplies a local tail-infimum proof over R and the coordinate reduction over C, rather than citing a B-page example.

contents.name: Theorem 16: completeness of bounded continuous functions, and c_0 exercise
contents.locator: printed pp.5–6, complete proof and final paragraph
contents.support: Adapt the coordinatewise unique-limit and uniform-Cauchy estimates to c_0 and supply the null-tail check; not a claim that the notes work out this exercise.

contents.name: Theorem 36: Uniform Boundedness Theorem
contents.locator: printed p.17, full theorem and proof
contents.support: Independent sequence formulation with Banach domain and normed codomain. Its Baire proof is comparison only, not an AC_omega proof. Do not copy slips: closure estimate says ≤1, not =1; union runs over all k; nonempty relative interior in the unit ball needs an ambient-ball refinement.

sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis, complete 563-page university-hosted manuscript
sources.locator: §4.1, printed pp.101–103 (PDF pp.114–116), from Baire category theorem through Corollary 4.4; complete relevant proofs read.

contents.name: Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2: Baire category and dense intersections
contents.reason: The text explicitly invokes choice for its recursive nested balls. Those results are comparison material, not suppliers for the AC_omega-only sequence proof.

contents.name: Rationals and irrationals category examples; meager and G_delta terminology
contents.locator: §4.1, printed p.102, intervening examples and prose
contents.reason: Category terminology and examples do not enter any owned claim; completeness failure is instead witnessed by the required explicit c_00 operator sequence.

contents.name: Theorem 4.3: Banach–Steinhaus dichotomy
contents.reason: The dense-G_delta alternative is stronger than the assigned pointwise-bounded sequence result and uses Baire. The extracted proof text displays slips (typeset-page screenshot retrieval failed): the union requires some alpha, and failure of density supplies a ball in the complement, not an open complement.

contents.name: Corollary 4.4: uniform boundedness principle
contents.support: Independent analytic theorem with exactly Banach X and normed Y. Specialize to a sequence; replace the Baire proof by the local Sokal adaptation and explicit axiom accounting.
